forces.title: Modular construction and prefabrication reshaping building product demand
forces.description: The construction sector is increasingly adopting standardisation and modular construction techniques, involving offsite fabrication of components. This structural shift, observed in large-scale projects, helps enhance productivity, improve quality, and ensure safety. For Building Products & Construction manufacturers, this necessitates a move towards producing prefabricated components and integrated systems, adapting to a future where onsite assembly of advanced modules is more prevalent than traditional build methods.
forces.source_title: Building India’s next 100 MTPA: Embedding execution excellence in steel project delivery

forces.title: Digital tools and AI driving smarter construction and building automation
forces.description: The adoption of digital tools like Building Information Modelling (BIM), drone analytics, digital dashboards, and emerging AI technologies is transforming construction project planning and execution. These technologies enable faster decision-making, greater visibility, and improved efficiency. For Building Products & Construction, this drives demand for integrated smart building systems, automated components, and solutions compatible with digital construction workflows, pushing manufacturers to innovate in building automation and digitally-enabled products.
forces.source_title: Building India’s next 100 MTPA: Embedding execution excellence in steel project delivery

forces.title: Government tax incentives boosting digital infrastructure and industrial manufacturing
forces.description: India's Budget 2026 introduced long-term tax incentives for data center and digital infrastructure expenditure. This policy is expected to accelerate digital transformation across industrial manufacturing, including the Building Products & Construction sector. By encouraging investment in digital infrastructure, the government aims to increase digitization momentum, foster technology adoption, and attract foreign partners, thereby creating a more favorable environment for innovation and growth in advanced building component manufacturing.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Industrial Manufacturing

forces.title: Accelerated AI adoption transforming industrial manufacturing operations
forces.description: Industrial manufacturing is witnessing rapid adoption of AI, with 59% of executives expecting deployment at scale within 12 months. This shift is driving significant financial gains through applications like predictive quality control (52%), downtime reduction (40%), and generative AI for product customization (38%). For Building Products & Construction manufacturers, this implies a fundamental change in production processes, emphasizing efficiency, quality optimization, and personalized product design through intelligent technologies, improving competitiveness and operational outcomes.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Industrial Manufacturing

forces.title: Data reliability challenges hinder effective AI implementation in manufacturing
forces.description: A significant challenge for industrial manufacturers adopting AI is the issue of data reliability, cited as a top risk by 76% of executives. Despite organizations believing they are building strong AI data foundations, inconsistencies and insufficient data quality can impede successful AI deployment and performance tracking. This poses a key risk for Building Products & Construction manufacturers in leveraging advanced technologies for operational efficiency, product innovation, and smart building systems, underscoring the critical need for robust data governance.
forces.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Industrial Manufacturing

forces.title: Robust growth projected for India's electrical equipment market
forces.description: The Indian electrical equipment market, a key segment for building components and systems, is expected to see substantial incremental growth of USD 76.24 billion (Rs. 6,44,533 crore) from FY24 to FY28, at a strong CAGR of 14.3%. This robust expansion is fueled by ongoing infrastructure development, industrial growth, and increasing demand for commercial building systems. The positive outlook provides a significant tailwind for manufacturers within the Building Products & Construction sector.
forces.source_title: Engineering And Capital Goods Industry In India

forces.title: Favorable government policies boost capital goods and engineering sectors
forces.description: India's capital goods and engineering sectors benefit from a liberal policy regime, including a de-licensed engineering sector and 100% FDI under the automatic route. The National Capital Goods Policy (2016) aims to significantly increase manufacturing share, production, and exports. These supportive policies create a conducive environment for industrial growth and investment, serving as a tailwind for Building Products & Construction manufacturers by fostering domestic capacity expansion and technological advancement.
forces.source_title: Engineering And Capital Goods Industry In India

forces.title: Massive Union Budget infrastructure capital expenditure fuels construction demand
forces.description: The Union Budget FY27 announced a substantial capital expenditure of Rs. 15.48 lakh crore (USD 172.00 billion) for infrastructure development. This significant government investment in roads, railways, urban infrastructure, and power projects directly drives demand across the construction sector. Consequently, manufacturers of building products and components, such as HVAC systems, prefab solutions, and various building materials, will experience strong demand growth as these large-scale projects move forward.
forces.source_title: Engineering And Capital Goods Industry In India

forces.title: Urban Infrastructure Development Fund to boost Tier 2/3 city construction
forces.description: The establishment of an Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF), managed by the National Housing Bank, aims to facilitate infrastructure creation in Tier 2 and 3 cities. This fund will support viability gap funding and enhance access to external financing for urban projects. This initiative acts as a significant tailwind for the Building Products & Construction sector by unlocking new markets and stimulating demand for building components and systems in rapidly urbanizing smaller cities.
forces.source_title: Engineering And Capital Goods Industry In India

forces.title: Strong credit growth in housing and corporate capex supporting construction
forces.description: The banking sector reports strong credit growth in retail (especially housing) and corporate capital expenditure segments. This robust credit flow, supported by RBI liquidity measures and stable deposit accretion, prevents funding stress and enables continued investment. For Building Products & Construction, this signifies a crucial tailwind, ensuring access to financing for builders and developers, thereby sustaining demand for building components, systems, and overall construction activity.
forces.source_title: Indian Banking Sector: Top Updates: Banking Sector RoundUp - H1FY26

forces.title: Workforce productivity revolution driving manufacturing operational efficiency
forces.description: India's manufacturing sector is undergoing a workforce productivity revolution, focusing on removing workflow inefficiencies, streamlining approval processes, and optimizing service delivery. This structural shift, emphasizing lean operations and efficient resource utilization, aims to achieve sustained productivity gains. For Building Products & Construction manufacturers, this implies a need to re-engineer processes, adopt better management systems, and invest in talent development to enhance operational efficiency and maintain competitiveness in a rapidly evolving industrial landscape.
forces.source_title: India’s trillion-dollar manufacturing ambition requires a workforce productivity revolution

forces.title: Data center expansion creates major demand for specialized building systems
forces.description: The rapid expansion of India's data center capacity to 7.0–7.5 GW by 2030 generates a cumulative construction opportunity of USD 30 billion by FY30, with specialized power infrastructure inside data centers alone valued at USD 18 billion. This creates a significant upside for Building Products & Construction manufacturers, particularly those offering high-specification internal power systems (UPS, PDUs, switchgears), advanced cooling, and integrated building automation (DCIM software) tailored for critical digital infrastructure.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

viewpoints.title: Government incentives to accelerate digital transformation in industrial manufacturing
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that the Indian government's Budget 2026 announcement of long-term tax incentives for data center and digital infrastructure expenditure will accelerate digital transformation. This is expected to attract foreign cloud service providers and boost digitization momentum in industrial manufacturing, including building products, where penetration is currently lower than international players. This policy support fosters investment in advanced technologies across the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: KPMG Global tech report 2026: Industrial Manufacturing

viewpoints.title: Modular construction crucial for enhancing productivity in large-scale projects
viewpoints.description: KPMG emphasizes that standardisation and modular construction, involving offsite fabrication and onsite assembly, are gaining traction. This approach significantly boosts productivity, improves quality, and enhances safety in large-scale construction projects, such as steel plant expansions. For manufacturers of prefabricated building components and systems, this shift presents a direct opportunity to supply more efficient, quality-controlled solutions to the construction sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Building India’s next 100 MTPA: Embedding execution excellence in steel project delivery

viewpoints.title: Indian electrical equipment market poised for substantial growth by 2028
viewpoints.description: The Indian Electrical and Electronics Manufacturer Association forecasts significant growth for the Indian electrical equipment market, including building systems. It is projected to experience an incremental growth of USD 76.24 billion (INR 6,44,533 crore) with a robust CAGR of 14.3% from FY24 to FY28. This strong outlook is driven by increasing demand across infrastructure, construction, and consumer goods sectors, indicating a positive environment for manufacturers of building components and systems.
viewpoints.source_title: Engineering And Capital Goods Industry In India
